name: Built to Spill
label: Up Records
lede: Doug Martsch wrote long songs so radio would ignore him, kept swapping bandmates, and still landed three records on Pitchfork's list of the 1990s.

eras.title: A Boise kid in a Seattle van
eras.text: Doug Martsch is 19 when he joins Treepeople, a Boise band that moves to Seattle and books punk bills instead of grunge ones. Three years in, he wants a band of his own.

years.src: Wikipedia: Treepeople · Seattle Weekly: Spilled history · Bearded Gentlemen: An Incomplete Guide To Built to Spill
years.h: Martsch becomes the fourth member of Boise's [[Treepeople|dec1aede-420e-4381-bfb7-e87ba02f25d6]]
years.p: Pat Brown, Wayne Flower and Scott Schmaljohn, all ex-State of Confusion, bring in Doug Martsch on guitar.
years.xp:
The band ends up in Seattle on C/Z Records, but Seattle Weekly notes it never sat in the Sub Pop grunge scene. Treepeople played all-ages bills with punk and straight-edge bands instead.

One critic put their sound between late-80s Hüsker Dü and the first Sugar album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Treepeople · Seattle Weekly: Spilled history
years.h: [[Treepeople|dec1aede-420e-4381-bfb7-e87ba02f25d6]] lose Wayne Flower, then Pat Brown
years.p: Martsch is left as songwriter in a band that keeps shedding its founders.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates Flower's exit to 1991 and Brown's to before the third album, Just Kidding (1993). Flower resurfaces in the [[The Halo Benders|859c297a-f739-45f2-ac58-401eeb2d017f]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill · Encyclopedia.com: Built To Spill · MusicianGuide: Built to Spill Biography
years.h: Martsch heads home to Boise and starts Built to Spill
years.p: The name came from a word game he played with his wife. The plan: he stays, everyone else rotates.
years.xp:
Martsch meant to be the only permanent member and pick new backing musicians for each album. He left [[Treepeople|dec1aede-420e-4381-bfb7-e87ba02f25d6]] in 1992, according to Encyclopedia.com and MusicianGuide. Wikipedia says the group ended in 1994.

The rotating-cast idea was dropped for about two decades, then came back. See 2018.

eras.title: A trio, a side project, and the record most people meet first
eras.text: Martsch debuts on C/Z with a trio, starts a side project with the man who ran K Records, then makes the record most people hear first. Up Records, a new Seattle label, puts it out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill · Bearded Gentlemen: An Incomplete Guide To Built to Spill · Encyclopedia.com: Built To Spill
years.h: Ultimate Alternative Wavers arrives on C/Z as a trio record
years.p: [[Doug Martsch|42c520b5-4992-4aab-9f3f-542addcde686]] plays with Caustic Resin's [[Brett Netson|7f1c14ad-ac89-46d7-9583-64dfb46f4fa7]] on guitar and [[Ralf Youtz|0fad8c79-2420-4758-b41e-207ba8dc136b]] on drums. Neil Young and Dinosaur Jr. are all over it.
years.xp: One guide dates the album to 1991. Wikipedia, MusicianGuide and Encyclopedia.com say 1993. Netson and Youtz were gone by the next record, replaced by Brett Nelson and Andy Capps.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Halo Benders · MONSTERFRESH: Unearthed Built To Spill / Halo Benders Concert From 1994
years.h: [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]] of K Records and Martsch start the Halo Benders
years.p: They trade verses and write separate songs. The first LP is God Don't Make No Junk.
years.xp:
Ralf Youtz, Wayne Flower and later Steve Fisk fill out the band. Unearthed video8 footage from the Capitol Theater in Olympia shows Built to Spill playing the still-unreleased There's Nothing Wrong with Love and then the Halo Benders taking the stage. The exact date is not settled.

Wikipedia also records that the band got pulled over in Utah in the 1990s while a crew was filming Real Stories of the Highway Patrol. They reformed for Boise shows in 2007 and a 2010 Olympia benefit.

years.src: Wikipedia: Up Records
years.h: Chris Takino and Rich Jensen open Up Records in Seattle
years.p: Built to Spill end up on its roster; the label will put out more than 100 releases.
years.xp:
Takino died of leukemia in 2000 and Pete Ritchey took over running the label. Its website stopped updating in 2007 and it wound down in 2008. Around 2018 its assets were licensed to Sub Pop, which now releases Built to Spill.

Modest Mouse, Duster, 764-HERO, Quasi and Tad were also on the roster.

years.src: Wikipedia: There's Nothing Wrong with Love · Encyclopedia.com: Built To Spill
years.h: Brett Nelson plays on his first Built to Spill record
years.p: Phil Ek recorded There's Nothing Wrong with Love at John & Stu's in Seattle between May and June. Andy Capps drums on this album and no other.
years.xp:
Wikipedia calls it a concept album about growing up. "Reasons" was written for Karena Youtz, then Martsch's wife, and "Cleo" is sung from the point of view of their unborn child. Encyclopedia.com says the song is about his son.

Singles were "Car" and "Distopian Dream Girl". Pitchfork gave it 9.3 and later ranked it 24th on its 1990s list. Sub Pop reissued it on vinyl in 2015.

eras.title: A major label that agrees to leave them alone
eras.text: A rarities collection, a benefit track, a summer tour and a three-album Warner Bros. contract all land in the same stretch.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill · MusicianGuide: Built to Spill Biography
years.h: A split EP with Brett Netson's band, plus a benefit track
years.p: Built to Spill Caustic Resin pairs the band with Netson's Boise group. "Still Flat" goes to the AIDS benefit compilation Red Hot + Bothered.
years.xp: Caustic Resin is [[Brett Netson|7f1c14ad-ac89-46d7-9583-64dfb46f4fa7]]'s band, from Boise. Netson returns to Built to Spill in the 2000s and plays on You in Reverse.

years.big: "I didn't want us to have a hit."
years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill · Wikipedia: Perfect from Now On · Consequence: Interview: Doug Martsch · Encyclopedia.com: Built To Spill
years.h: Warner Bros. signs a band that would rather not have a hit
years.p: Martsch says he wrote long songs so radio would leave them alone. The deal: three albums, health insurance for a newborn son part of the reason.
years.xp:
The deal, per Wikipedia, was three albums with real creative control. Martsch has credited the band's lawyer, who had worked with R.E.M., Sonic Youth and Dinosaur Jr. He said: "I don't know why they let us do what we do, but they have."

Wikipedia reports the health-insurance motive, tied to Martsch's newborn son. Scott Plouf, a former Spinanes drummer, is the drummer by now.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lync · Encyclopedia.com: Built To Spill
years.h: The Normal Years gathers the singles and odd tracks
years.p: Lollapalooza and a European run supporting the Foo Fighters come around this time.
years.xp: Wikipedia's [[Lync|65e1b41c-c719-4237-9f72-c2f07ea19355]] entry says the Olympia band's bassist James Bertram and drummer Dave Schneider joined Built to Spill as touring musicians, as documented on this release. Sources differ on whether the Lollapalooza dates were 1995 or 1996.

eras.title: Long songs, then short ones
eras.text: Perfect from Now On is the anti-hit. Its follow-up, with Brett Nelson and Scott Plouf writing alongside Martsch, comes closest to being one.

years.src: Wikipedia: Perfect from Now On
years.h: A hot car ruins the first take of Perfect from Now On
years.p: Heat damages the master tapes on producer Phil Ek's drive from Seattle to Boise. The failed attempts cost $20,000.
years.xp: Wikipedia's account has three sessions. Martsch first plays nearly everything but drums himself, and he and Ek both hate it. The second attempt, with Nelson and Plouf, is the one that gets cooked. [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]] encourages them to try again.

years.src: Wikipedia: Perfect from Now On · Encyclopedia.com: Built To Spill · Consequence: Interview: Doug Martsch
years.h: Perfect from Now On: seven of eight songs run past six minutes
years.p: Warner Bros. debut, finished at Avast! in Seattle. Pitchfork ranks it 22nd on its 1990s list.
years.xp:
By February 1999 it had sold 43,000 copies, according to Wikipedia. Encyclopedia.com puts it at about 40,000.

Martsch later told Consequence the band grew out of the rotating-cast plan around this record because he wanted "more collaborative music".

years.src: Wikipedia: The Halo Benders · Consequence: Interview: Doug Martsch
years.h: Halo Benders put out The Rebels Not In
years.p: It is their third and last K Records album, after God Don't Make No Junk (1994) and Don't Tell Me Now (1996).
years.xp: Martsch told Consequence that attempts at new Halo Benders material later sent some songs to Built to Spill.

years.src: Wikipedia: Keep It Like a Secret
years.h: "You Were Right" strings together a classic-rock jukebox
years.p: Martsch built the song from lines by the Rolling Stones, the Doors, Jimi Hendrix, Bob Dylan and others, and Warner secured the clearances late.
years.xp: That is how Martsch explained the method. Wikipedia says Warner cleared the copyrights at the last minute.

years.src: Wikipedia: Keep It Like a Secret · Wikipedia: Built to Spill · MusicianGuide: Built to Spill Biography
years.h: Keep It Like a Secret makes the Billboard 200
years.p: It debuts at No. 120 and sells 60,000 copies in its first year, per Wikipedia, on shorter songs than the last record.
years.xp:
Martsch said he was burned out on long songs. The band held week-long jam sessions in Boise with him triggering a tape deck by foot pedal, then he mined the tapes. Tracking began in November 1997 at Bear Creek in Woodinville, with overdubs at Avast! in mid-1998.

Pitchfork gave it 9.3 and named it 1999's best album. Karena Youtz contributed lyrics, according to MusicianGuide.

years.src: Wikipedia: Treepeople · Bearded Gentlemen: An Incomplete Guide To Built to Spill
years.h: Pat Brown, the Treepeople bassist, dies
years.p: Wikipedia says he died by suicide in 1999. One guide places it two months after Keep It Like a Secret.
years.xp: Martsch dedicates the 2006 album You in Reverse to Brown.

eras.title: Martsch goes short, then goes solo
eras.text: Built to Spill puts out a live double and a record of three-minute songs, and Martsch cuts a blues album on his own.

years.src: Seattle Weekly: Spilled history · Bearded Gentlemen: An Incomplete Guide To Built to Spill
years.h: Ancient Melodies of the Future runs 40 minutes with no long songs
years.p: A deliberate return to the shorter pop songs of There's Nothing Wrong with Love, after the live album Live (2000).
years.xp: Bearded Gentlemen's guide calls "Strange" the band's best pop song.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill · MusicianGuide: Built to Spill Biography
years.h: Martsch makes a solo record, Now You Know
years.p: Blues and folk, with Delta blues the reference point in one bio.
years.xp: Built to Spill goes quiet while it comes out. From 2003 to 2005 the band tours 150-plus dates.

eras.title: Two years on a shelf, then a bad spring
eras.text: You in Reverse finally comes out after two years on a shelf. That spring Martsch's retina detaches and Andy Capps is found dead.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill · Consequence: Interview: Doug Martsch · Bearded Gentlemen: An Incomplete Guide To Built to Spill
years.h: You in Reverse sits on a shelf for two years
years.p: Four guitarists, including [[Jim Roth|cc7cb41f-c7c3-4ad3-916e-bf139a9c7ab4]] and [[Brett Netson|7f1c14ad-ac89-46d7-9583-64dfb46f4fa7]], record it in Portland in 2004. It is dedicated to Pat Brown.
years.xp:
Martsch told Consequence that he and engineer Steve Lobdell made it at Audible Alchemy in Portland. It was less collaborative than he wanted, with less jamming time.

One reviewer calls it a "Television album": long interlocking guitars, back to extended songs.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill · Bearded Gentlemen: An Incomplete Guide To Built to Spill
years.h: The band tours again after Andy Capps dies, and dedicates "Car" to him
years.p: Capps was found dead in his Idaho home on May 18. Martsch also had retina surgery in March, which cancelled South by Southwest.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band dedicated performances of "Car" to Capps. He had played drums only on There's Nothing Wrong with Love.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill
years.h: Bob Odenkirk directs the "Hindsight" video
years.p: There Is No Enemy comes out first, and the clip follows a year later. Wikipedia calls the album the band's highest-charting.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the tracklist as revealed August 17, 2009 and "Hindsight" released as the first single September 8. The video, directed by Odenkirk, is dated September 2010.

eras.title: Eighteen years in, the rhythm section walks
eras.text: Brett Nelson and Scott Plouf are out. Martsch, Jason Albertini and Stephen Gere make the last Warner album as a trio.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill
years.h: A secret Portland show debuts a new rhythm section
years.p: Jason Albertini (Helvetia, Duster) on bass and Stephen Gere on drums play Bunk Bar by invitation. Nelson and Plouf's exit is announced January 7, 2013.
years.xp: Martsch later said an album made in 2012 was abandoned because of the departures and his own dissatisfaction.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill
years.h: Sam Coomes co-produces a trio record, Untethered Moon
years.p: Martsch, Albertini and Gere make it, with Coomes of Quasi, a frequent touring keyboardist, behind the board.
years.xp: Netson and Jim Roth left in the second half of 2015, and a three-piece debuted in spring 2016.

years.h: After 22 years, Warner Bros. and Built to Spill part ways
years.p: The split is announced with no new label named.

eras.title: Martsch goes back to his first plan
eras.text: He says out loud that the band is returning to the rotating cast he started with. It is a Sub Pop band now, and Treepeople get back together.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill
years.h: Martsch announces a rotating cast for every record, again
years.p: Brazilian musicians João Casaes and Lê Almeida become the rhythm section for South American dates.
years.xp: Martsch posted it on Facebook. By 2019, Melanie Radford was on bass and Teresa Esguerra on drums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Treepeople
years.h: Treepeople reunite with Troy Wright on bass
years.p: The original lineup returns with Wright replacing Pat Brown. The reunion ends with a final tour in August 2023.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the final tour covered the Pacific Northwest and Idaho.

years.h: Built to Spill cover Daniel Johnston for a whole album
years.p: Built to Spill Plays the Songs of Daniel Johnston is covers, not new material.

years.h: Sub Pop signs Built to Spill
years.p: The label that reissued There's Nothing Wrong with Love on vinyl in 2015 becomes their home.

years.src: Wikipedia: Built to Spill
years.h: When the Wind Forgets Your Name is the first new songs since 2015
years.p: Recorded before COVID with Casaes and Almeida as the rhythm section.
years.xp: Sub Pop released it. It is the band's first album since Untethered Moon.

years.h: Thirty years on, There's Nothing Wrong with Love gets played front to back
years.p: The anniversary tour starts in August with Yo La Tengo.
